newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen in range but vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen in range but vulnerable.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE cocoa futures are seen steadying after losses last week that pushed July down near its April 9 low of 980 stg a tonne, analysts said on Monday.
But the market was not yet clear of another speculative attack, traders said.
July cocoa was called to open down five stg, in line with New York's slightly softer close on Friday. CSCE July ended down $6 at $1,413.
"It's basically in a ranging phase, but there is more downside in the phase rather than upside," said Cornelia Dichio, analyst at Chart Watch.
She said the range was clearly marked, with London July resistance at 1,060 and crucial support at 980.
London July slid last week to re-test 980, but the level held again to form a triple bottom on daily charts. The 980 level was the April 9 low. On May 1 and June 5, the low was 981.
Triple bottoms normally indicate strong support that can serve as a base for a rally, but traders and analysts were not yet convinced in this case that level would continue to hold.
Fears of more speculative liquidation lingered over the market, they said.
After Friday's market close, the CFTC's latest commitment of traders report showed 16,369 non-commercial longs and 16,058 nonr-eportable longs in New York. Both were up from the previous week.

In addition, traders here said London speculators were also net long, despite massive liquidation last week. Some estimated speculators and funds still had a few thousand contracts to liquidate in London.
They said those sales could help push July through 980 and then attract new sales.
Next major support was not expected until about 950.
